key_insight: Phase-adapted shallow neural dictionaries achieve an N^(-1/2) Sobolev approximation rate, while matching a chirp signal’s phase reduces the phase-dependent growth of the proven error upper bound.
engineering_relevance: For oscillatory one-dimensional signals, incorporating known phase structure into neural features can yield sharper approximation guarantees than using mismatched features.
method: Define weighted modulation spaces using the short-time special affine Fourier transform and relate them to classical spaces through chirp factorization.
Construct a transform-adapted neural dictionary and prove bounded-domain and global N-term approximation estimates.
Analyze matched and mismatched dictionary phases for fixed-scale chirp families.
evidence_signal: Four numerical experiments examine model comparison, dictionary-size error decay, phase mismatch, and restricted-translation obstruction; these diagnostics are distinct from the theoretical best-approximation estimates.
watch_item: Global guarantees require unrestricted translations; phase-mismatch comparisons concern upper bounds, not optimal-error thresholds, and the sine branch loses rank at zero phase.
paper_title: Weighted STSAFT-Modulation Spaces and Approximation by Phase-Adapted Neural Networks
